<description>
The double spend case in `TestBasicMining` is meant to check that block template creation fails when two mempool transactions spend the same coin. It reuses the transaction from the preceding coinbase case, whose prevout was cleared with `SetNull()`, and only overwrites the prevout hash. The output index therefore stays `COutPoint::NULL_INDEX`, so both transactions spend an output of `txFirst[0]` that does not exist.

Set the output index to 0, so the first transaction is a valid spend and only the second one makes fail.

Found while working on #36692 and https://github.com/yuvicc/bitcoin/pull/19.
</description>

<commits>
b2c7f2545e test: spend an existing output in TestBasicMining double spend case

The double spend pair reuses the transaction of the preceding coinbase
case, whose prevout was cleared with SetNull(). Only the prevout hash
was overwritten, so both transactions spent output index
COutPoint::NULL_INDEX, which does not exist. Template creation
therefore failed on a missing input even without a second spend.

Set the output index to 0 so the first transaction is valid and only
the double spend makes template creation fail.
</commits>

index 6ff1788b1b..faa8362910 100644
--- a/src/test/miner_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/miner_tests.cpp
@@ -546,6 +546,7 @@ void MinerTestingSetup::TestBasicMining(const CScript& scriptPubKey, const std::
 
         // double spend txn pair in tx_mempool, template creation fails
         tx.vin[0].prevout.hash = txFirst[0]->GetHash();
+        tx.vin[0].prevout.n = 0;
         tx.vin[0].scriptSig = CScript() << OP_1;
         tx.vout[0].nValue = BLOCKSUBSIDY - HIGHFEE;
         tx.vout[0].scriptPubKey = CScript() << OP_1;

</patch>
